subject: language
intro: I'm Ms. Kim, 8th grade ELA. Let's plan a lesson on how a theme develops across a text.

beats.narration: "Tracing" signals that theme develops over the whole text.
This standard asks students to analyze a theme's development over the course of a text.

beats.text: Students will be able to state a theme as a complete sentence and trace how it develops through the characters, setting, and plot.

beats.narration: This makes the difference between a topic and a theme clear.
beats.text: "Friendship" vs. "True friends stand by you even when it costs them something." "Which one is a theme? Why?"
Model finding a theme in a short story by tracking what the main character learns. Use a chart to show the theme at the beginning, middle, and end.

beats.narration: Group agreement pushes them to debate and refine the theme.
beats.text: Groups read a short story, agree on a theme statement, and trace it at three points in the story with evidence.

beats.narration: The ending is often where theme is clearest.
beats.text: Write a theme statement for today's story and give one piece of evidence from the ending.

outro: Topic vs. theme, model, trace, check. Now plan yours.
